direction.more_critical: adds or strengthens a charge or negative characterisation of Israel or Zionism, or removes Jewish-history or self-description framing
direction.less_critical: the reverse: removes or softens a charge, or restores Jewish-history or self-description framing
direction.neutral: wording, grammar or links only, with no change in stance
direction._extension_for_oct7_articles: For Hamas, October 7 attacks and Gaza genocide the same axis is read from Israel's standpoint in the conflict: more_critical also covers removing or softening a charge or negative characterisation of Israel's adversaries (e.g. terrorist, massacre, hostage-taking, militant); less_critical is the reverse.

voice.own_voice: asserted by the encyclopedia as fact
voice.attributed: assigned to someone, or hedged ("scholars describe", "critics say", "has been described as", "alleged", "according to")
voice.na: no claim changed; also used when a claim is removed and nothing takes its place

claim_type.verifiable_fact: a date, event, place, number or organisation name
claim_type.contested_characterisation: a judgement disputed in reliable sources, e.g. colonial or colonization, settler-colonial, ethnic cleansing, apartheid, genocide, terrorist, massacre, re-establishment, homeland, national liberation

axes.uncodable: Either the before or the after wording was not stored (or the stored text is blank, i.e. the sentence was emptied), so the change cannot be judged from the texts.

more_critical.tradeoff: "More critical" is closest to the codebook but reads as a verdict on the editor; "adds or strengthens a criticism" is descriptive but misses the removal-of-framing cases, and "less favourable to Israel's framing" covers those but is longer and centres one party.

less_critical.tradeoff: Mirror of the above; "closer to Israel's framing" captures restored self-description but can be read as "pro-Israel", which the code does not claim.

neutral.tradeoff: "Wording only" is the most literal; "no change in stance" states the coding judgement openly; "tidy-up" is friendly but may understate edits that move facts.

mixed.tradeoff: "Mixed" is short but vague; the long form is clearest for readers but does not fit a chip.

own_voice.tradeoff: "Stated as fact" is plainest; "in Wikipedia's own voice" is the term Wikipedia itself uses and is hard to dispute; "unattributed" is precise but negative and less familiar.

options: with a named source or hedge
attributed.tradeoff: "Attributed" is exact; "alleged" must be avoided because it implies doubt the text may not express; the quoted form is vivid but only fits "according to" phrasings, not "has been described as".

na.tradeoff: "No claim changed" fits wording edits but is wrong for removals; the removal wording is accurate only for that subset, so a page may need two labels.

verifiable_fact.tradeoff: "Checkable fact" says why it matters but implies it was checked; the enumerated form is unimpeachable but long; "factual detail" is soft and may understate events.

contested_characterisation.tradeoff: "Contested label" is short but "label" can sound dismissive of terms some scholars defend; "disputed description" is neutral; the long form names the test (dispute in sources) but is wordy.

na.tradeoff: "Style only" is reader-friendly but slightly overstates (links and grammar too); "no substantive claim" is exact but abstract.

method.coders: Two blind passes, each a separate headless Claude process with no tools and no access to the repository, given only masked pairs (A/B order randomised independently per coder, a flag for which came first; no ids, dates, counts, revert flags or article metadata) and the identical codebook. Third pass: adjudication of disagreeing axes only, with a note per transition. Agreed axes stand as coded. Then a mirror check: where both A->B and B->A were coded, the directions should be opposites; 4 adjudicated codes were changed to match a mirror both coders agreed on; residual mismatches between two agreed codes are listed in mirror_check and left as coded.
method.unit: distinct (from wording, to wording) transition; codes are then mapped onto every page change k (tl[k-1] -> tl[k]).
